messages:
Jesse: Heads up — Borealis pilot hitting repeated 429s during warmup, started ~10:15 PST. Landing page demo flows are failing. Can SRE triage? @Marco

Priya: Saw it too, just on a call with the customer. They're running a 2k-user warmup script. Quick Q from the customer: is there a recommended warmup cadence to avoid rate limits?

Marco: Looking now. Initial grep shows 429s from /v1/generate, backlog on the swarm. Sampled logs: ```[2026-03-20T17:15:03Z] req_id=0x9a7b status=429 reason=rate_limited route=/v1/generate tenant=borealis-726 tokens=48```

eng-bot: alert: average 429 rate 12/min on cluster-redwood-7. autoscale triggered x3 but queue still building.

Lee: Is this hosted or Dedicated? If hosted we can apply a temporary burst policy (allowlist) while they warm up.

Jesse: Hosted. Customer is on trial credits and just asked about pricing if we need to bump capacity during the POC.

Anya: I'll check pricing ops — we can offer a one-time trial burst credit. @Priya can you confirm expected qps during peak?

Priya: They said ~120 rps for 3 min bursts, then ~10 rps steady.

Marco: That explains it — current per-tenant rate cap is 50 rps. Options: increase tenant cap, route to Dedicated pool, or suggest client-side backoff w/ jitter. My recommendation: temporary cap bump to 200 rps for 90m to allow warm cache/KV.

Jesse: Customer wants minimal config changes. Can we do a cap bump quickly? Also need eng to monitor KV cache warms during the run.

Marco: I can lift the cap now for tenant_id=borealis-726. Applying in ~1m, will watch heatmap and logs.

eng-bot: action: rate_limit_override applied -> tenant=borealis-726 new_cap=200 rps by Marco at 1918123600

Anya: Thanks Marco. Priya — tell the customer to run warmup at 60 rps for 5m first, then spike to 120 rps. That should avoid queue overflow and limit 429s.

Priya: Sending that now. Also asking them to share the exact warmup script and expected demo cadence. They also asked for a short note on SLA and data isolation during trial.

Lee: For trial, clarify data is processed on hosted infra but isolated per-tenant; share the security FAQ: https://redwood.example/security/pilot-FAQ (internal link).

Jesse: FYI, customer saw a secondary 503 when model fallback triggered. Any logs around that?

Marco: Found fallback events at the same times. Looks like the primary model variant wasn't warm in-region -> auto-fallback to smaller variant, which spiked CPU and yielded 503s. Mitigations: pin model variant, pre-warm model cache, or allow cross-region routing. Opening an infra ticket now.

Marco: Created INFRA-989: investigate regional model cache warming for tenant borealis-726. CC @Lee.

Jesse: Timeline? Customer needs resolution before tomorrow's demo at 09:00 PST.

Marco: I'll prioritize. ETA for initial mitigation (cap bump + model pin) ~2 hours. Full infra fix (regional cache strategy) ~24-48h.

Priya: Customer accepted the temp plan and will move the demo to avoid the initial spike window. They'll confirm in ~10m.

Anya: I'll draft the incident notes and update the POC tracker (sales-poc/borealis).

Jesse: Leaving this thread as the single source of truth until the demo completes. @eng-bot please post metric snapshot at +15m and again pre-demo.

eng-bot: ack — scheduled metric snapshots at +900s and at +28800s (pre-demo).

Lee: One more ask — sales wants a pricing note for a short Dedicated burst vs hosted overage. @Anya can you pull current short-term Dedicated burst rates and expected latency improvements?

Anya: Will pull and DM pricing. If they convert to Dedicated we can show clear cost/latency tradeoffs and a path to guaranteed capacity.

Jesse: Thanks all. Quick status recap: cap bumped to 200 rps, infra ticket INFRA-989 opened for model cache warming, warmup cadence shared with customer, demo tentatively rescheduled. I'll update exec thread after demo.
